posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
I'm not even slightly joking when I say I've been waiting for those Isolated Hero rules for years.

If GI Bunker uses his innate power on a target, and an Isolated Hero deals damage to that target, the damage is not made irreducible.

Mr. Fixer is an Isolated Hero and plays Grease Gun. When a non-hero target tries to deal damage to a hero target, and cannot, this does not count as “affecting another hero."

Suppose Haka has some of Unity’s cards (typically, mechanical golems) under Savage Mana, and then Haka or Unity becomes an Isolated Hero. If  Haka uses the power on Savage Mana, the Unity cards are not destroyed. They stay under Savage Mana.

Here are the most relevant rules from our long-since-dead-but-never-forgotten thread on Isolated Hero back in the day.

Edit: I STILL don't know about Stun Bolts and Isolated Hero. We used that example a lot in the above thread, but these Fireside rules don't quite address the Stun Bolt interaction. MP, can you shed some light on that one?

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
f Guise uses “Lemme See That” to take “Jack Handle”, and then uses “I Can Do That, Too” to use the power “Squall," then for each target hit by the power, Jack Handle takes effect. For example, if there are 4 targets in play, Guise will deal 1 damage 4 times each to the 4 targets (16 times in total). Gross.

WHAT?

 

Okay, Poop just got extremely real.  So, essentially, any time a card other than Jackhandle would cause Fixer to deal damage to a target, he deals that damage to all non-hero targets instead.

And Dual-Crowbars, anytime a card other than itself (meaning that card, not excluding other dual crowbars) or Jackhandle cause Fixer to deal damage (I'm countinng the first damage as being the original hit even if that isn't technically correct) you deal another target that much damage.

 

So Fixed Point+Jackhandle+Dual Crowbars+Blackout is the real deal.  (just not in the video game yet)
